query: I have $8,000 spread across three credit cards at 19%, 22%, and 24% APR. What's the best way to pay this off?
atoms: perspective: Motivation-driven borrower needing quick wins
perspective: Good-credit borrower eligible for balance transfer
plausible_answers: Answer A (Avalanche Default): Pay minimums on all cards and throw every extra dollar at the 24% card first — the avalanche method minimizes total interest and is mathematically optimal for someone committed to following through.

Answer B (Snowball for Motivation): Target the smallest balance first regardless of rate — the psychological wins from eliminating individual cards keep most people on track better than pure math, making snowball more effective in practice.

Answer C (Balance Transfer): Transfer all three balances to a 0% APR card and pay off the full amount within the promotional window — if you qualify, this eliminates interest entirely and is faster than any payment-order strategy.
baseline_answer: Answer A (Avalanche Default): Pay minimums on all cards and throw every extra dollar at the 24% card first — the avalanche method minimizes total interest and is mathematically optimal for someone committed to following through.
